utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, let me -- sorry. Let me explain to you first that this is not a special report from CC Mostar and from the M1 team what exactly describes the hijacking of the car. It isn't. Let me explain you the first page, and that makes clear where it comes from. It comes from the head of the regional centre, Zenica. So this is the French ambassador at that time who is responsible for this summary of his whole region. And one of the communications centres within his region was Mostar. So this is not our report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But in order for your boss in Zenica to be able to create a summary, he needed to receive reports from various teams in the region. So probably your boss then compiled a summary and forwarded it -- I mean, your boss in Zenica - that was Mr. Thebeault, if I'm not mistaken - he would receive reports from M1, M2, M3 teams in the field, and then he would compile this summary and send it onward. How else would he have known about the situation in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Absolutely, you are right, but this is sent to the head of mission in Zagreb, as you see, and it's his responsibility what he writes in his report. So we don't have anything to do with him. We only gave him our reports, and he is free, and it's up to him what he writes to the head of mission. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] Right. [Interpretation] We will go back to that, but we just found a document that refers to the mujahedins, and I hope that Madam Registrar has found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies. I had started on one document, and since the witness reminded me that the incident in question was a car-jacking, I wanted to bring in a document which further clarifies that incident, and I did not mean to create any confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So Witness, since I already asked you and I was advised by my colleagues that since we were dealing with one document, perhaps we should finish dealing with one document at a time. So my apologies to you, too, if I created any confusion in your mind. So let us finish off with the report of the head of mission. What I wanted to ask and what refers to the Mostar region or province here, were they called provinces because of the Vance-Owen plan?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, which document are you talking about? Which one of the two?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It's my fault. It's my fault, Witness, and I apologise to you. I went back to the first document because I thought that -- I thought it more sensible to finish dealing with that first document. Then we will move on to the document to which I referred subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. It's my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, now, do you want us to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 431. 431 is the one that I would like to finish dealing with. We started dealing with it, and I thought it better to finish with it, and I apologise to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What I'm interested in in regard of this report, it's on page 3, the last sentence, it is the Mostar province, which states -- [In English]: "Committed by Croats..." Sorry. "Committed by Croats irregulars in the nearby villages of Sovici, Doljani burnt out by the Vlado group." Vlado in this case is a given name rather than the word for the government in Croatian, which is also similar; it's Vlada. Is this the summary that has been compiled here based on the reports received by the M1 or M2 teams which then Mr. Thebault could summarise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, can you refer to which part of the document we're supposed to be looking at because neither Judge Liu or I can find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I was reading from Document 431, page 3. There's no Croatian translation of this; it's only in English. And the ERN number is 00594704.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It is the last line of the Mostar province report. Following that, there will be the report marked 3, which is the Zenica province. I don't know if you were able to find it now.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just waiting for Their Honours to find the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I just say, Mr. Krsnik, what I'm looking for is something in that report that's relevant to the hijacking of a car. Isn't that what I'm supposed to be looking for?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is the Exhibit 431. It is the Exhibit 431, and the car-jack report is Exhibit 485. What I was referring to was the Exhibit 431, page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Referring to what event?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These -- this is a description of the events in the Mostar province, region. And the sentence that I had read was the last sentence that refers to the Mostar province in that report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was addressed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: These reports regarding the Mostar province -- I mean I was only interested in this last statement from the report. I just wanted to ask the witness, this is a joint report by M1 from Jablanica and M2 from Mostar. Were Ambassador Thebault's sources the reports of these teams? I mean, in order to verify this document, right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, in principle, he got the information by our CC reporting system, but it's very hard for me, and you will understand that, sir, that I can't give comments on reports I didn't wrote, were not written by one of us. And we are also not responsible on this level about what is written in this report. So it's hard for me to give comments on that. But in principle, from our region, from CC Mostar, he got the information he used for his interpretation of the situation, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. That's precisely what I had intended to ask you. I am satisfied with your answer. If it had to do with the Mostar province, you would be the one who would have to provide information about this. Thank you. And now we are going to slow down a bit. We can now move on to Document 485, which is right in front of you. Document 485, page 10. Page 10, that's what it says in the upper right-hand corner. M1, Jablanica, and then CC Mostar. Is that correct? That page, I mean.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Does this give a description of what happened? I think that it was a matter of kidnapping your vehicle, looting, et cetera. Is that what's described here?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, it seems to describe what happened, but this is still not the M1 special report. This is also not coming from CC Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Number 1, special report, right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, but that covers more subjects than the special report I'm talking about. The special report I'm talking about is a special report made by one of the members of that team. And he describes exactly what happened, and it is not this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It also has to do with theft, kidnapping, et cetera, so this is a different event altogether. That means that there were several occurrences of this nature; that is to say, thefts of money from your teams, I mean, if I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, when you want to stick to this event, you need, I think, to have the basic document to get a very clear picture of what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I absolutely agree with you. However, unfortunately, I haven't got this document, so I've tried to do my best with the documents I have. This special report I have here refers to that -- I mean, if you've read it, you will see it that it says that the members of your team were robbed, et cetera, if I'm not mistaken, by the BiH army or rather members of the BH army in that area.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, there are some facts in this short part what I recognise as being in the special report of the team. But you have to compare it because I think that the special report by the team member is the most valid one when you want to know what happened actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I agree with you. My final question, Witness -- I hope that I've understood you properly. What you can confirm are the CC Mostar reports, right, that is what you can confirm in the sense of your own reports. I mean, those that Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 7472 to 7491. you can confirm as being authentic reports that are your own, the CC Mostar reports?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, I think to clarify the situation, my reports and my statement has to do with M2, the team in Mostar. This is -- or the special report by M1 is written by M1, and I can't comment on such a report because I was not a part of the team. So I hope that you understand that I want to stick to my own products.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: By all means, Witness. That's precisely what I have been trying to say. Perhaps we in the courtroom think a bit differently from you soldiers. You have to say certain things in court, and I have to put questions to you in order to get these answers. So you can confirm the authenticity only of the CC Mostar reports, or rather concerning places where you were, right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, I do, but you can see it because it's written on top that it's from the ECMM mission, it's a report of the ECMM mission. So no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Certainly. You see, through you, Witness -- I'm sure the Trial Chamber will allow me to explain this to you -- certain documents were being introduced through you. So we can only introduce those documents that you confirm as being authentic. So perhaps the Defence is going to call some of your co-workers in order to verify some documents if my colleague, the Prosecutor, doesn't do it before me. So thank you for your patience and for your answers. Let me go back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have been quite patient for some time but I'm afraid that there may be some mischaracterisation here unless I make a comment on this last point for the record. This witness, I submit, respectfully, has never said that he is not in a position to authenticate, for instance, other ECMM documents. What he has been careful to say, and I submit properly so, is to not speculate about the content of the reports of -- other teams' reports. But I fear at some future date we may hear from counsel that this witness has said something about not being able to confirm the authenticity of a number of ECMM documents. I submit, Your Honours, that that's not what this witness has said. He has, in fact, just indicated a moment ago that he can clearly corroborate that particular document. It's clearly an ECMM report from the head of RC Zenica, Ambassador Thebault, and he said that. And it's not fair to the witness or to the record to suggest otherwise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, your remarks is recorded correctly in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, of course I don't want to take up Court time, and I don't want to create a certain kind of atmosphere in this courtroom because I see that we are all a bit over-saturated. This was not my understanding of what the witness had said. I have dwelled on this subject for quite some time with the distinguished witness. I think that all of this has been recorded in the transcript, and I don't want to engage in any kind of repetition because -- so I disagree with what the Prosecutor just said, but after all, it is for you to judge, so let me move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, we shall move on. Your time is precious as well. Have you ever seen Mr. Mladen Naletilic in the Ministry of Defence in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you ever see his name on any door in the ministry. You personally, have you ever seen that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Negative, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So the belief that his -- that he might have an office in this building comes from your interpreter. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That was one of the sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: But it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: -- it was confirmed by others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please. These others who confirmed this, they saw my client's name on a door in the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I can't answer this question. I don't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, yesterday you testified about an event that took place in Mostar on the 30th of June, that is to say, when the BH army launched a major offensive when they attacked Bijelo Polje, the northern camps, Sjeverni Logor, and they were preparing to attack Rastani, which they indeed did two days later, so this was a comprehensive military action on the 30th of June. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We heard that on the west side but we were not able to check it because our freedom of movement was by the first checkpoint denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Weren't you in Mostar on the 30th of June?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, but we came not further than the hospital, as you could read in the daily report. And then we went to the place where the interpreter was living, and that was all. The rest was impossible. The access to, for instance, the east side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Would it be fair if you confirmed to me that when such major military operations are involved, that the side that you are on should take care of your security in your capacity of guest, observer? I mean, what would be strange if they took care of your security and safety? Imagine what would have happened had something happened to you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Let me make this very clear: Freedom of movement had nothing to do by taking care of security, in this case, of our team. In fact, we were responsible for our security, so they had to let us through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Had something happened to you, Heaven forbid - and thank God nothing happened to you - who would be responsible? If something happened to your team - thank God nothing did in this war chaos - who would be responsible?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: ECMM, sir, and common sense by the team members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Oh, all right. Thank you for your answer. So when this military operation was taking place, you testified yesterday that you encountered Mr. Andabak, that he was excited. Tell me, if such large-scale military operations were underway, is it strange that soldiers should be excited? I mean, they could get killed any minute. They go into these operations every day.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Not at that spot, sir. That spot was HVO controlled, the west side. He was excited and angry because he didn't expect us to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That is your arbitrary conclusion. Can you agree with me on that, that is what you inferred?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That was -- that is what I observed, that is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, well, wasn't all of Mostar a war zone?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: What I said before, there was some parts well controlled by HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, how many times did you meet with Mr. Bruno Stojic, Minister of Defence, in your report I think it says three or four times that you had two lengthier conversations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I think at least four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When you met him in Siroki Brijeg, you wrote a very long report on his viewpoints and you found out from him, if not then on 30th, what actually had happened on the 30th of June in Mostar. As a matter of fact, you included this sentence: "Our assessment was that Bruno Stojic takes the military and political situation very seriously." That is your statement on page 21, I think, in your version. "In my opinion, the HVO did not -- was not concerned about the situation before, but now they really were worried." Then you got a complete military picture of the military operation that was taken by the BH army on the 30th, they took all of Bijelo Polje, the hydroelectric power plant, Rastani, and they were preparing to penetrate the centre of Mostar, and I am going to find your original report for you, in addition to this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, what's your question, Mr. Krsnik? You have to ask a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was waiting for the witness to read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, is this --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: You are talking about page 20?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Of the Croat translation. In English, it is page 21, the entire page refers to your meeting with the Defence minister, Mr. Bruno Stojic. You met on the terrace of a restaurant in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: What do I have to read? Especially what do you refer to from that page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, sir. I read something, and it's only fair for you to read this together with me. That's why I meant that you should have a look at this page and read it. I thought that you would read it yourself.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I'm ready for your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did Mr. Bruno Stojic make this military statement, so were you informed about the complete military situation in Mostar as of the 30th of June? Did Mr. Bruno Stojic inform you about it or not?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Without any doubt, because this is my statement, and it comes from my daily reports. I made it myself, so... Positive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What's strange about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I thought counsel was going there, but if it assists, it's Exhibit P497 is the report of that day which covers this conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, first I read out from the statement that the witness made to the OTP, and now I have document 497 in front of me. In the statement he made to the OTP, Your Honours, the witness extensively referred to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: As for this military and political situation, was it explained to you as well by Mr. Jadranko Prlic at the meeting you had with him when he was president of the HVO, I think this was on the 2nd of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, he made a statement that covers also the concern at that moment. And you can read that in the daily report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when speaking to the mayor of Siroki Brijeg, Mr. -- well, you called him Ivo Culic, did you get a complete picture -- I see this in your report so I'm just asking you for confirmation -- how many refugees there are in Siroki Brijeg, what kind of difficulties they're facing, and that six Muslim refugee families live together with Croat families.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: This is what he told us, yeah, that we were always verifying to our best knowledge, verifying this kind of information from other sources, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So did you check this piece of information?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, we tried to check it, of course, but was hard to do that at that time, at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you hear of the Muslims having any kind of problems in Siroki Brijeg? Did you hear about that personally or from several sources?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Point 8, I see that you usually give assessments. "It seems that in the HVO zone, they are taking good care of all refugees and displaced persons." And then you continue: "However, reality on the basis of many examples shows a different picture." First you state that they take good care of them, and then you say that there are examples that prove otherwise.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, to clarify this, I think that the first statement was what we heard by the officials, the official authorities. And our assessment was always the combination of what we heard from the officials and what we saw ourselves. So the assessment was the responsibility of the team, and the interpretation of everything what happened and what we heard and what we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In Siroki Brijeg, did you personally ever see Mr. Naletilic with a bodyguard, as you had put it yesterday? Or was it only in the car?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We saw him in the car with bodyguards, and we saw him in Siroki Brijeg also with people who accompanied him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, how did you infer that the people who were in the same car with him were his bodyguards? Was the car just standing there or was it driving by? I mean, was the car moving or was it just standing there?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Once we passed him by the checkpoint, I could see what kind of people were inside, of course. He was in the back seat. And, well, heavily-armed, angry-looking youngsters, sometimes they called them bodyguards. So by our best knowledge, it looked to be bodyguards or personal staff, as you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would suggest that we take our break perhaps two minutes earlier than usual so I could consult my colleagues in order to conclude my cross-examination as fast as possible. I have just completed a particular topic, and I would only have a few questions after the break, and that would conclude my cross-examination altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can I ask you how long you are going to take for this witness this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that it would not be more than half an hour -- I mean, that would be my maximum, half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, and how about Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I expect to take less than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just wanted you to know that we have to finish with this witness today. Mr. Usher, would you please show the witness out of the room first. We'll resume at 2.30 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.58 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Having consulted with my colleagues, we have reached a position that we have exhausted all the questions that we had of this witness. I would like to thank him for his patience; and I wish you all the best in your life. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Van der Grinten - and I apologise if I mispronounced your name - I am Branko Seric and I represent Mr. Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the usher's assistance to show the witness a binder that was shown to the witness by the Prosecutor yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you to find P454.2 -- 452.1, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was told that there was a different number. Yes, it's the correct number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, I apologise if I repeat questions, but there was something I did not understand. Who provided you with this list?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: A man in the western part of Mostar stopped us -- stopped our Jeep and gave this note, telling the story about expelling people the previous night and gave this by saying these were HVO soldiers involved in the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: According to the evidence you gave, you received this on the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, it is stated in my daily report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What does this mean, this appendix of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues...]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you explain why the attachment -- actually, there's an attachment at the bottom of this. What is that attachment?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: You mean number 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Not under 6, but this attachment here.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That was -- that is the writing of the investigator, so I suppose that this belongs by another thing what is numbered as you see in the attachment. So this is not my handwriting; this is from the investigator. So everything in black ink except attachment PB A909130801, and the two small paragraphs at the right, except that, the rest is my handwriting. Okay. And one of the paragraphs is also mine, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Fine. Did you learn what was the man in question, who it was who had given you this piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I don't know his name, but according to the message he gave us also verbally, I made this note as you see. So the writing list of HVO soldiers who expelled Muslim people on the 13th about 17.30 hours is mine own handwriting, and I wrote this on the piece of paper after the interpreter inside the car translated the story the man told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you verify the authenticity of the information given you by the man?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, of course, we tried to figure out if the story was true by the various other international and non-government organisations, like Red Cross, UNHCR, and the day after, actually, on the 15th, we received the official protest letter with attachment from the other side. So there were actually several sources who confirmed this first message.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: The copy that you have in front of you, is this the actual size or is it enlarged? In other words, is that the same size of the paper that you received?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I have to be careful now because the original is here, but this is, of course, a copy of the original, and if it exactly fits, I don't know. But the original paper from more or less this size is here; I brought it to the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you know the ethnic background of this informer who provided you with this piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No. I don't know his name; I don't know his background.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So whatever this man told you on that occasion, you learned from the interpreter, male or a female interpreter, I don't know which interpreter you had at that time.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, as I said, this paper was given through the window by the man, and he told a story about it. He explained what it means. And that was, of course, translated by our interpreter to explain what the story was. And according to that story, I made this note. And, of course, he was not mentioning all the names of the expelled people, but he said exactly what I stated in my statement. And that statement is based on our daily report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: We will come to your special reports a little bit later, but let me ask you something else first. What I'm interested in is whether you can tell us whether the man who provided the paper was an eyewitness or perhaps the interpreter could provide that information?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, I can't answer that -- that question at this moment because I don't know it and can't recall it at this moment after eight years.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you can remember because a lot of time has passed. Did this man say in which street this had happened?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, but I can't recall the place where it happened. But it was on the west bank. That's what I know for sure. You find that back in the daily report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you recall today, and I apologise for insisting so much on it after so many years, but on the basis of the story that you heard through the interpreter, how far those expulsions were from the actual spot from the location where he provided the paper, when he gave you the paper? Was it in the same street where he gave you the paper, was it in another neighbourhood, in another part of town?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Other part than what -- that what part you mean? You mean if it was on the spot where it happened? I don't understand your question, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: My apologies. At one point, this man came and stopped your vehicle in a street. Now, do you recall today where this was? Was this going on in the same street where the man stopped you, several streets away, or was in another part of town?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't recall that. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let's go to the Exhibit 456.4, please. This is a letter of protest, and I have four pages, and I believe you should have four pages, too.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you agree with me that on page -- that page 1 contains the text of this protest?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: The written text, I think it's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that this body of text is in English language, the first page?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that the next page is in Croatian or Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, there is a translation in English, but the names, of course, are in -- in the Croatian language, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: At the very top, it is written in Bosnian the list of refugees who were expulsed on the 13th of January 1993 until 2200 hours. And it lists not --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: At the very, very top, you see the translation in English, and that was on the original document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I must admit that I don't see it in my copy.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, it is there in my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, if you turn over to the next page, which should be page 3, and at the top you'll see a number "2" for pagination.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I see. I have it here in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On that page, do you see anywhere anything written in English?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Not on this copy, but you have to see the originals to be sure. But it's possible that there was no English on that second page. That's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I, too, would like to see the original so we can compare it. Now, on the following page - which, as you turn over, if there is no pagination any more, it should be either page 3 or page 4 - you have the list of names. My copy such is that I really cannot see it, but is there a page number on that page?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, not on this one what I have in front of me, but this is a copy of the copy, so it's not the original page, of course. It could be possible that there was no number on the original one, but it's better to check the original than asking me, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I agree with you, but I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, no objection, Counsel, but I just thought it might assist. Your Honour, I've sent an inquiry out of the courtroom to see if the original can be brought to the courtroom. It was one of these documents which is on this old-fashioned thermal fax paper which fades over time. And if it's available to us, we'll have it brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also like to thank my learned friend Scott. It would help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But what am I driving at? What I would like to get from you through my question is when we see, just as a physical set, does this appear to you as one complete, whole document, these four pages?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: When you see the original ones, the original copies I have to say, then you see that there are, let's say, documents written on the same typewriter. I'm not a specialist. But even as non-expert, I believe that the four pieces of paper belong to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Doesn't it not look to you that the last page was somehow added on, that is, why -- or to put it this way, why are the pages not numbered sequentially 1 through 4?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, actually, you are asking the wrong person because I was not -- I was provided with the papers, but I didn't wrote them. To explain to you once more, we got the original ones, consisting of the protest letter and three additional pages. And because of the thermal paper eight years ago - and it was in my file as copy - after eight years, it became hard to read. And that's the reason that -- and this is, again, my handwriting you see here on the back of the last page. That is why I wrote, after making a dark copy, the names as I could read it on the last page. But the four pages were delivered at the same time to us on the east side at the HQ of, I think at that time it was General Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Grinten, you are right when you said these were not appropriate questions for you, but this one is: Did you understand this letter of protest as -- for what it was, that is, as a letter of protest or did you see it as a potential piece of evidence?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, actually it was a confirmation of the message we had before, and all we heard from the other organisations. So at that time, not knowing that I should sit, after eight years, in this court, I was not considering that as evidence for this case. But it became evidence, actually, by the originals, let's say by the copies I had in file. And at that time -- let me make it very clear, at that time when we received on the 15th these protest letters with additional pages, it was in confirmation of that what we heard before. And as I told you before, that was very important in our work, not only dealing with rumours, but get confirmed information from different sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: We heard that you received this letter dated the 14th June, the protest letter, that is. You also said that on the 14th, the unknown man, you received the piece of paper on the same day.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. The protest letter of General Pasalic was given on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: No, I was referring to the date. If you open -- if you go to page 1, it was dated 14th June.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, that's correct, but we didn't receive it on the 14th. According to my daily report, we received it on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did it cross your mind that both may have come from the same source?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That was very unlikely in the situation. I don't think so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you compare the typeface created by the typewriter on the piece of paper and the letter? I know you're not an expert, but some things can simply be seen by looking at them.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, sir, you gave the answer yourself. I'm not an expert, and what I stated in my daily report about the time -- the day/time group we are talking about, the day, the time, and the hour for so far that was mentioned, it's according what happened. So I don't have any more to say as nonexpert, and I think that my daily reports makes very clear when we received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, I would like to move on to P476.2. Please look at the signature -- rather, there is no signature. It just says the place, Ilici, and the date. Will you agree with me that it says the 24th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I think that you have to go to the second page because that is -- I'm sorry, you have to go to the third page because that's the original document in the Croatian language, yeah. Because this, where the exhibit number is on, is the translation of our interpreter. She translated the Croatian text, as you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You're right, you're right. On the top of the page it says, "02083633," and the date is -- thank you, thank you. Again, you'll have to go back to the English translation because you don't know Croatian. It says, "[Come to Ilici]," it says, pardon, in parentheses. "Last night a crime was committed there." According to the text, does it mean that the crime was committed on the 23rd of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, then, I have to go to the text very carefully because I can't remember that exactly, of course. But it says "Last night," so that makes sense. Then it was last night, the night before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let us perhaps even be more specific. Do you remember the time of the day when this little piece of paper was handed over to you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Unfortunately not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I repeat the question. According to the text of this information, this little piece of paper, would it mean that this event had occurred on the 23rd of June, 1993? Because in our terminology, in the Croatian language, if something happened on the previous day, that is yesterday, yesterday afternoon, last night, yesterday evening. There is a difference between yesterday evening and last night, you see.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Of course there is, but I think we have to stick to the original document, if there was a misinterpretation. Well, I don't know, and I can't recall that. And I'm not a specialist, once again, when we are talking about translation from the Croatian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now move on to your information with regard to this event. This was compiled on the 25th of June, 1993. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: You mean in our daily report?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes, your daily report.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Let me check it because I don't know the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: That is P477.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I have the document here in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In the Croatian version, it is page 2; in the English version, it is page 3. This is what it says. This is the daily report from the 25th. Let me just have a look at the English. In the Croatian text, it is paragraph 4; and in English, it is the fourth and fifth sentences. And this is what it says: "However, we saw a few soldiers that were placing death notices for three Muslims who had died yesterday." "Yesterday," it says. The daily report is dated the 25th. "Our interpreter confirmed to us, she said to us that those three were the family that was referred to in the note." I think that there is something illogical here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not going to, I guess, object to -- again, I don't think counsel should argue with the witness in that way. But while on my feet, I can tender to counsel through the usher, with his assistance, these original fax pages, if that might assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. I'll take the opportunity to remind Mr. Seric about the fifth line from the top of this page. It was written there that one Muslim family was burned in their house two days before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, Your Honour, this is what it says, that the interpreter confirmed that those three were the family that is referred to in the note, the three who died, yesterday. I am speaking about the death notices and that particular piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: My question is whether it is one and the same event.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: But you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In terms of the note.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. When you are talking about the text on top of page R0162814, and that in accordance with the note, then we are talking about the same event. So the text on top what says that the Muslim family was burned in their house, then we are talking about the note in the Croatian language we just saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, then, what this particular part of your daily report means, that is, sentences five and six? "The interpreter confirms that it is the family to which the note refers."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think Mr. Seric is making the point to which he attaches a great deal of importance, apparently, that the note that was given to you by the child refers to an event which occurred the previous day. By the time you received the note, the event was two days old. And that when your interpreter looked at the documents that were posted onto the tree, they referred to a death that had occurred the previous day. So Mr. Seric is attaching a great deal of importance to the fact that the death notice on the tree referred to a death that occurred one day previously, and the note you received occurred two days previously. I think the Court has that point, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. So I have no further questions in this regard, then. I shall go back to the other documents. I do apologise to the Honourable Trial Chamber. I will kindly ask the usher to show this to the witness. We have two pages here. There is no pagination, but it is after the protest in English. I don't know whether it is the second or the third page. On the top of the page, there is no English translation, and on the other page there is. The second page, the page numbered number 2, continues in Croatian, then the fourth page, without any pagination, is in English again. In the copies, you can't really see this. So this is the whole set, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When you look at this really, I have only one single question left, and that will conclude my cross-examination. Did you check this information that you received?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, when you look to the top of the pages, you can see that they are all coloured the same and that a staple is removed. These are the original ones, with a translation in English on the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: We will really have to get an expert for documents because on a few pages, there's no English translation on the top. All right. The Trial Chamber will deal with this.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: You are asking me what is my opinion, though. My opinion is that these here, these four, where the staple is removed, I think for the copier, are the original ones. That's what I recognise being in my file. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm not challenging any of this, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions. Perhaps if there's still something that is hanging in the air, so to speak, perhaps you could instruct me if I should clarify some further points. But basically, I feel that I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Seric, if you've asked, I'm wondering about the quality of translation on a few documents which were translated possibly by interpreters who are not of the same calibre or quality as interpreters that we have here. The word in the documents, the note that was given to Mr. Van der Grinten by the child referring to the death by fire, if I can find it now, that is translated as the flat having been mined in English. How do you translate that from the Serbo-Croatian language note? The note that is Exhibit 476.2, Mr. Seric. There's a translation in English, and then the original note that starts with, "Help me..."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it now. In Croatian, it says, "The house had been mined."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: For the record, I asked does "minimana" [phoen] mean mined?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As if an explosive device had been placed underneath the house, that is. It doesn't have to be a mine, you see. In our language, it does not literally have to be a mine in our language. It can be any explosive device.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's the point I was making. Mines being placed around the house seems a little old-fashioned. So the word in Serbo-Croatian, if I understand you exactly, means an explosive device. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Your Honour. I wonder if the documents -- I wonder if those documents could be provided to the Chamber just so -- because the Chamber will have some idea as to what the material looks like. It's impossible to copy without running into the same exact problem. I'll just pause, Your Honour, until the Chamber has had a chance to just quickly look at them. Mr. President, while the Chamber is doing that, perhaps the usher and the registrar could assist me by giving two numbers, whatever the next exhibits numbers would be in the Prosecution list, to these two photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P893 is the next number, and I will mark this vehicle, the photo of the vehicle, as P892. And the next exhibit is a photo of a building, and that will be P894.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You skipped 3. You seemed to skip.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Oh, I'm, sorry, P893 is the vehicle, and P894 is the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Colonel, just very quickly, because I didn't anticipate that your cross-examination would dwell so heavily on some of these matters. If you could look first at the photograph that has been marked first as P893, and since at the moment there's only one in the courtroom, if that could just be put on the ELMO, please. Is that a copy of the armoured four-wheel-drive vehicle that you used during your tour in Bosnia in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In this particular photograph, only very briefly, can you point to the Chamber to show on one occasion one of the bullet impact marks that had occurred prior to this photograph being taken?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah. You see here the impact of the bullet that hit the car on the 3rd of June driving the car from the west to the east bank in advancing the Tito bridge actually. That is the impact that we are sure of that was fired from the blue bank building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And during the time of your tour in Bosnia-Herzegovina, did your vehicle always appear that way, including the bright orange letters EC monitor, and the blue symbol, if you will, of the European community or the European Union?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We always drove this car with these signs upon it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can ask you, please, then, to turn your attention to Exhibit P894. If that could also be placed on the ELMO, please. The taller building in that photograph that we see, can you identify that building, please.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, sir, that is the building we called in our reports the blue bank building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And approximately where was that in relationship to the confrontation line in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That was very close, actually very close to the confrontation line on the west side, west bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm finished, usher, with those two photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, just so the dates are clear, Colonel, is it correct that your tour of duty began on approximately the 24th of May, 1993 and continued until approximately the 22nd of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: When you are talking about leaving the area, that's correct, the 21st. When you are talking about entering the Mostar area, that was late May, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Because my whole tour was longer, of course, but not in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't mean to say ECMM such as in Hungary, but your time in Bosnia-Herzegovina was approximately from late May to late August?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, some of the names you have mentioned, Colonel, if I might, because questions have been raised about the source of your knowledge and the people you dealt with while you were there. Did you meet with Bruno Stojic, the HVO Minister of Defence?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct; several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You testified today that you met with him at least four times?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: At least. I think it was more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you have any meetings or dealings with a man named Slobodan Bozic, the deputy Minister of Defence?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We met him also when Mr. Bozic [sic] was not available.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This man Stanko Maric, a senior HVO officer, how often did you meet with him, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, it's hard to say, but I suppose more than ten, maybe 15 times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you meet with Valentin Coric, the head of the HVO military police?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We met him at least, at least two times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you meet with Mr. Burko Pusic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We met Mr. Pusic more often. He was the deputy of Mr. Coric. When Mr. Coric was not there, then we addressed Mr. Pusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say "the deputy," he was the deputy head of the HVO military police?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You've indicated you met with this man Jadranko Prlic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was his position?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: He was the president of HVO, by my knowledge, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You met with this doctor, the head of the west side hospital, Ivan Bagaric. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Approximately how many times did you meet with him?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Four or five times maybe. I don't recall it exactly, but at least four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You met with a man named Slavko Puljic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Puljic, yeah, at the -- on several occasions, most of the time at the HQ of HVO, and I remember that, in the beginning of June, during the joint committee meetings, he was also there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what was his position or title, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I think that he was a local -- no, he was in the beginning. I think he was, in the beginning, chief of staff from HVO army. Later on, he became commander of one of the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And by way of summary, approximately how many times did you meet with this Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: At least three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Ivo Culjic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: The mayor of Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, how many times did you meet with him?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: At least three times. I think more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you meet with a man named Darinko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, he was in charge of the Bosnia/Croatian refugees and displaced persons. And by my memory, we visited him at least once in his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And finally, did you ever meet with a man named Kresimir Zubak?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: At least once.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall his position?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: He was, I think at that time, the vice-president.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Colonel, the testimony that you provided to this Chamber in the last two days in your evidence, is much of that evidence based on your meetings and dealings were all the individuals you've just named?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, actually, strictly upon our daily reports, and daily reports were made after, directly after the meetings, returning from the meetings or the end of the day, returning to our place, our CC in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just about two or three more questions. Can you tell the Chamber, please, how would you compare the extent of destruction in both parts of Mostar? And when I say both parts, the east and west side, and I'm directing your attention away from the immediate confrontation line and putting aside clearly that both sides of such, for instance, the Bulevar were badly damaged. Once you got away from the confrontation line itself, how did the destruction in West Mostar compare to the destruction you saw in East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, the eastern part of Mostar was actually in extended -- looks like an extended confrontation line when you compare the damage with the western part of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how would you compare the situations that you found at the hospital in East Mostar compared with the HVO hospital in West Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, by our visits of the western hospital, we actually entered a normal organised and working hospital. And on the East Bank, we called it the war hospital. It was not in a regular hospital building, but I think in -- it was an old school or library or something like that. I can't recall exactly. But the building was not suited for a foreign hospital, of course. They were operating, for instance, in the kitchen of the building. And also the space was, of course, not enough, and not a lot of things was arranged at that particular place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Colonel, I thank you again very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from Judges? Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes, Colonel, I have some questions for you. I have quite a number, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'm going to go chronologically through your evidence, and there are a number of items I wanted to have clarified, so possibly I'm going backwards. You described in an early stage of your evidence a man who was well known in the area as Juka. And today, you couldn't remember his name, but yesterday you described him as Juka Prazina.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, because I had the document in front of me, and it's easier to -- for me, to read his name from the paper than I recall it after eight years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I accept that totally. It happens to us after only one day. Colonel, does the name "Prazina" ring a bell? Are you satisfied that Juka is Juka Prazina?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: On the day that Juka Prazina tried to disrupt a meeting that was taking place with General Pasalic and you, do you remember if he was dressed in a uniform?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: He was dressed in a uniform at that time. Or, let's say, a kind of uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did your information or information gathering inform you as to what Juka Prazina's background was? Was he a career soldier or somebody who took up a uniform and a gun?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, of course, we had some background information from UNPROFOR and from our own organisation. So we were, I think, well informed about the men who were operating in that area, or could -- let's say, the people we could met in that area sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court what your information on Juka Prazina was in relation to his background and his military training, if any?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, actually, the most important information we had was that he was acting previous in Sarajevo as a commander of also a special unit. And the information also was well known that he was not educated from scratch as a military man. By our information, it was one of the guys who took advantage by the conflict to act as, between brackets, a "military commander."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Would you like to say, Colonel, who the other men were who also took advantage of the conflict to act as military commanders?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: One in our information was Mr. Tuta.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And what about Mr. Andabak?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Of course Mr. Andabak, but I already mentioned that yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: This leads me to my next question, which happens to follow also the evidence that you gave. You informed us yesterday, and you translated to a certain extent for us this series of documents which are described as the HVO command structure, and you led us through that document, and you told us that this was based on what you considered to be very accurate information garnered by SpaBat --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: At that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: -- And UNPROFOR. I have been looking through the documents and with your assistance obviously can understand it a lot better. This evidence is unchallenged evidence, and if I bring you to page 5 of that document, which deals with the SPF. Now, I think it would be of assistance if you had the document in front of you. It would be possible for the Prosecution to furnish you with the document. The registrar has done it.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Do you have the document which has two rectangles coming down from a line called "SPF"?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, the question that I want to ask you is, where the SPF derives its authority from and where does it fit into the command structure?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, actually, you need an additional page because you see -- we are talking about page C4 or 5, is that correct, just before, "UN restricted"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, as you see, there is a line between the two boxes that gives the regimental size, that depicts regimental size, Mostar and Grude, you see that there is a commander relationship by the line above, but we need -- actually, because this is, let's say, a -- this is a part of the whole -- what we called organigramme and you need to follow that line to find who was, let's say, the chief of the both commanders of the special forces. So I think that I have to look for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes, I would like your assistance on that.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: We have to go back to explain it a little bit better. Page A3, when you go back, page A3, and I'm mentioning the numbering of the UN, that is, as you see, the political organisation, you have to go back -- six pages actually back. Then the next page is, let's say, the agenda about the symbols, and then you find, "UN restricted," page C1, the HVO military structure but within Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the interesting part then, for your question is, of course, the most left -- left box. That's called, "Southeast Herzegovina, Mostar on Charlie 1." Because the other operational zones, "OZ" stands for operational zones, are in other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So when we focus on Mostar, then we go to the next page, and there you'll find the most left block broken down in smaller units. And as you see there, you find in the breakdown of this picture, again, a box with a cross on top. That means brigade size, brigade size, called Mostar. You see the commander and the deputy commander. There you find Mr. Pusic we are talking about. So breaking down that organisation is done on page -- is done on page Charlie 4, actually, you find the back, that's done on Charlie 4 Alpha. When you see page Charlie 4, you see by the Mostar brigade number 3, so the 3rd Brigade southeast, Mostar, you see the grid where it was located. VH 2898, Commander Ivan Primorac, deputy commander Mila Pusic. And when you go now finally to the page you started with the special forces, you see that Mostar and the grid is the same, VH 2898. That means that the line actually has to -- has to be drawn as it is by the other two brigades on page Charlie 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So does that mean, Colonel, that if we're looking at what you called Charlie 4A, where you have the parallel line at the top of the page with two verticals leading to SPF -- Mostar and SPF Grude, that we should draw a vertical line upwards joining up with the hatched rectangle which says "Mostar" and underneath it either a Y or a VH 2898.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, it's a Y, not a V. It's YH 2898, that's correct. That means that, in simple words, under the brigade, you'll find a special forces unit from regimental size, and that was broken down in two units from company size, and then we are -- then we are at Commander Juka and Commander Andabak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And if we move upwards to Commander M. Naletilic, Tuta, do we come to Pusic and then Primorac?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. Colonel, do you make a distinction between special forces and paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Not in this organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So in a number of your reports, you refer to Mr. Puljic, or Puljic, referring to paramilitary organisations, and I think maffias, which have capos. Are you talking about different words for the same thing?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Definitely not because here we are talking about uniformed soldiers, I'm talking about the army. And that's exactly the most important difference between -- when we are talking about our descriptions in the daily reports, and we are talking about these units, then we are talking about HVO army, uniformed soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think you misunderstood me. When you are talking about the special forces who are described in the document there, and then later on in your reports you talk about paramilitary units, are you talking about the same people?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The paramilitary units are different people from the special forces?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: When we are talking about paramilitary units, we are not talking about uniformed units within a structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So can I read from that, or if I understand you correctly, the special forces were uniformed units within a structure?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That was as we described it, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I refer you to your report towards the end of the book of documents. It's Exhibit 484. It's a report of the 29th of June, 1993. And if I can bring you to the third page, which is entitled "R0162829."

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: In particular in that report, you're talking about the concept of exchange of doctors between the west and the east side, and you have written: "When we asked him about the exchange of doctors with the east side, he liked the idea. But he told us that some paramilitary organisations still existed in the community of Herceg-Bosna, and they are putting a lot of pressure on the HVO to avoid any agreement with the Armija." Who was he talking about when he talked about paramilitary organisations, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, that's very hard to say, Your Honour. Actually, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And then if I take you to the next page, which if I understand your evidence correctly, the part called the assessment is your own personal view based on the various pieces of information and intelligence which you've received. You said that, "Mr. Puljic appeared to be more friendly than his HVO colleagues and also more honest. We think he has told us the truth when talking about the paramilitary organisations inside or next to the HVO." Now, you go on to say that: "These organisations are extremists and nationalists, usually full of criminals from all over the world. Their power is their money and their behaviour worse than any other people." Are those a reiteration of his views or is that your assessment?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Assessment was ours. As I told before, after meeting him, we put everything together and made also our own comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And then the next: "Their power is their money and their behaviour worse than any other people. We had met some of these capos of these maffias (Mr. Tuta, Mr. Andavac, Mr. Yuka, et cetera, et cetera)..." Again, is that your assessment or are you reiterating his words?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No, that was our assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, if I go to a different subject, I appreciate that after the end of June, that your access to the city and close environs of Mostar was extremely limited. But before that, for the six-week period that you were there before that, were you able to ascertain where in the area of Mostar were Muslim refugees housed or was there a reception centre for them?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Not by my knowledge. Do you mean on the west bank?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes, on the west bank.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Not by my knowledge, on the west bank. Then only the Heliodrom, but that was, by our visits, a prison, not what you mean, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: What I mean by a "reception centre" is really a refuge for them where they were treated in a humanitarian fashion. Was there a reception centre anywhere in Mostar for refugees, either Croatian, Serbian, or Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: At that time, not by our knowledge, by my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did anybody ever suggest to you that Muslims were being removed from premises which were not theirs and the premises were being given back to their rightful owners?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: West bank, you're still talking about? This is actually the first time that I heard that suggestion, here in the courtroom this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You also said that when you were investigating reports of Muslims having been removed from their residences, that you went to the places and you found that there were stickers on the door. Could you give me a little more information about what sort of stickers they were?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: What I saw that were HVO stickers, stickers from HVO units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: What did they say?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I don't recall, but most of the units had patches on their uniforms with a symbol what showed, for instance, to which unit they belong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I understand you now. I thought it was a sticker from the HVO with an announcement, but it was a sticker which represented a particular unit formation.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's what I saw myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Maybe, Your Honour, I can make it a little bit more clear about the assessment you just mentioned. The problem we, of course, had was that, for instance, Mr. Tuta, we never saw in uniform. He was in the military organisation, by our knowledge, but we never saw him in uniform. By coincidence, mentioning the 30th of June, we met Mr. Andabak in uniform but never before. That Mr. Juka normally also was changing from civilian sometimes to uniform. So that made it actually very complicated, and we had, of course, some information about the background of the gentlemen. So you have to put this text in that context actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you about Mr. Bagavic, I think. Bagavic or Bagaric.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Bagaric, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Ivan Bagaric. You described yesterday that he wasn't quite the picture that you had in your mind of what a chef de clinique ought to look like, and in particular, you said that he had a camouflage jacket and was carrying a pistol under his white coat.
