Do you know if this man was actually in fact a medical doctor or was he merely the manager of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, he said to us that he was a doctor. But the only thing we recognised, actually, was the white coat. It looked more, actually, a military man with a white coat on. But he told us that he was doctor, so...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: He told you that and you also know he was in charge of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Seems to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You'll be glad to know finally I'm coming to the end of my questions. I think you described that you met Mr. Andabak, who is reported or referred to as "Andavak," and you explained that the Spanish spelling of "B" is "V." So --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I don't know if that is the case in the Spanish language, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Well "Valencia" is pronounced "Balencia," et cetera, but you said it was a mistake in the Spanish spelling. You said you met him three times and you described how you met him once when he was angry and he was excited and you explained the circumstances. Did you ever meet this same man, Mr. Andabak, officially?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, I think that the only time that we met him officially was by surprise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So on the other occasions, was it a chance encounter?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: In Siroki Brijeg, and I think once downtown Mostar, from the three times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: There's just one question I should have come back to at the beginning that I should have asked you about. Early on in your evidence - and you were cross-examined about this - you described how you had information that Mr. Tuta had an office in the department of Defence building, and that this information was confirmed by your interpreter. I particularly looked this up, Colonel, because you were cross-examined on the basis that you were told by the secretary first. But am I correct in interpreting your evidence as having been that you heard from other sources first that Mr. Tuta had an office, and the office was pointed out to you by your interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: It is the last situation, because we were well informed by our predecessors about the situation and what we should see at the MOD, the Ministry of Defence, by our first visit. So...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Colonel. You have been very patient with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Clark. Judge Diarra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My questions have already been asked, actually, by my colleagues. However, I would like to ask the colonel what kind of unfortunate actions could specifically be given to the special units that were directed by Juka and Andabak and headed by Mladen Naletilic. Just tell us, please, about these unfortunate actions led by these men on the ground.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, we had the impression that their task was, for instance, expelling people, intimidation, threatening, looting. It happened always at night in darkness, and it was always what we called covert actions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Diarra. Any questions out of Judges' questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, we did not question any of the documents simply because this is not a set compiled by this witness, he just accepted it on its face value. We will file separate documents discussing this, the documents of the SpaBat cannot be entered in this way and we will provide arguments for this. The documents and the charts that he now talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Colonel, I'm going to ask something on the basis of the questions of Judge Clark. Do they have something like a tactical groups, special units, that is, that are sent for especially dangerous tasks? Do you know if there is an equivalent between such units and what you have?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Can you be more specific? Can you mention the unit, for instance, because I don't understand quite well what you're asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This is a follow-up on Judge Clark's question. These special forces that are mentioned on page C4A. Can they -- do they have the same name in the royal army or is that identical to, say, tactical groups? Can special forces be called tactical groups and the special forces as described here are identical to the ones in the royal army?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, I explained to you before that that comparison is not valid because I don't understand what you mean. Of course, special forces is used according to the type of organisation and the nation in different ways. It doesn't mean always the same. You see the special forces of the U.S., the U.S.A., are tasked in another way than, for instance, the Dutch battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, if I understood you correctly, I'm going to try to show the chain of command like this, and let's say this is the HVO headquarters. This is where the commander and the chief of staffs are. If we drop one line below, they had four operative zones, Mostar, southeast, southwest, and northwest, as the four main areas. Now, we are not military experts ourselves, but below the Mostar operative zone, we have the next level, which is brigades, and then below that there would be special forces. So in terms of chain of command, he would be on the eighth rung. In other words, he can act only if he has orders of eight superior officers. In other words, it is conceived in the headquarters, then it is sent to the sector to which it refers; in this case, Mostar, and then the Mostar operative zone implements the plan and sends it down to the brigade, and the brigade uses special forces as needed. Was my understanding of what you said correct? And also, based on the chart that you interpreted for Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm still looking at the chart myself, and I still have it pasted together here. I think it's not fair to put that question to the witness without having it in front of him again, because if you just go through the layers, you can count them. And I think the witness ought to have this in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The witness has these charts in front of him. He interpreted them for Judge Clark. I'm just trying to confirm whether my understanding of what he has said here is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll work on the chart in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I basically copied it based on what the colonel said.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Such a diagram shows the chain of command normally, that is the need of such a picture. It is showing the chain of command, who are in charge of who.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is my sketch, then, correct, the one that I drew? Did you agree with it just a moment before? If we have the headquarters, which is the main headquarters, which is superior to the four commanders of four operative zones. Do you follow me? Now, the Mostar operative zone has a brigade, and below the brigade is the special forces unit.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Belonging under the brigade you find the two units, let's say, first the regimental special forces unit and then the two from company size, that's correct

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, Colonel, usually any action is conceived at the headquarters, any operation during wartime at the headquarters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Well, depends how it is organised because every level has a certain responsibility within their area of operations given by higher command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: After that, it is sent down to the main commander of one of these zones; in this case, the Mostar operative zone, the southeast zone. They implement the orders, and also send them down to the brigade, and the operative zone will decide whether and where they will use special forces. Is that correct, in military terms?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That could be the situation. It depends, it depends, how it is organised, of course, and that's not everywhere the same. It depends on the nation, for instance, and the way the army is organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Colonel, I'm going to show you another chart. I wasn't -- I hadn't intended using them but since you introduced them. Look at C5, please. Charlie 5 is closer to NATO terminology, I guess. You have northwest Herzegovina operative zone, and again you have a commander of special forces, and again it's Ivan Andabak. Colonel, same rank as the other one; it's him again. How is this possible now, that he was both in Mostar and in this -- in the northwest Herzegovina operative zone? And thirdly, in all your reports, you described him as an -- as the overall commander of all special forces of the HVO, which is what you confirmed to me when I asked you, you confirmed that I had asked you whether Mr. Ivan Andabak in your reports is named as the commander of special forces. That was today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think that's a mischaracterisation of the evidence. He was a special commander. I think it's a stretch to say what Mr. Krsnik has just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. My colleague will find where I asked it, and I think that we will all see that it is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I have to remind you that we are about 15 minutes behind our schedule. You must finish your question as soon as possible because I understand that there are a lot of documents to tender through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honours. However, the questions of Judge Clark we perceive as very important, and we would like to clarify them fully. [In English] Line 15, page 26 [Interpretation] The question was -- the question was, "Will you please tell me whether your statement and your reports --" is it true that in several places, at least in three places, in your statement and in reports, you said that Mr. Andabak -- you say, "He," but it's in reference to Mr. Andabak -- of the HVO. Answer: "That's correct."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's not, "Overall Commander." "Commander" and "Overall Commander" are two totally different concepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, commander of the special units of the HVO is, it is self-explanatory. These are the HVO special units. There are no other ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't think -- the witness doesn't -- forgive me, I don't want to interrupt Judge Diarra. The witness does not have the ability to scroll back, but in looking at that, it says exactly -- our record at least, I don't know, maybe Mr. Krsnik and I are not looking at the same page. It says, "A commander," I believe, which is what the transcript says and which is what I recall. "A commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's, "A commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is letter "A."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There are a lot of commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I will ask the tape so that I can see what I had asked in Croatian, because I remember quite well what I had asked, because I based it on the report where it stated clearly. I don't know whether this witness can come back tomorrow morning. I'm going to show him in three places, on three reports, where he said -- he wrote down that Ivan Andabak was commander of the special forces of the HVO. This I drew from the reports of this witness. And I wanted to just compare this to -- with this page C5. And I haven't received the answer to that yet. Plus, in Mostar operative zone, he was a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, That would have been a company-sized unit in this chart?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: No, no, no, maybe I can answer and help you with this misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: What I said in the beginning, according to this diagram, that we had this information and that Mr. Andabak was one of the commanders of a special forces unit. And you see on this diagram that -- on the diagram is commander of a company-sized unit. And I never said that he was the only one in charge of special forces in Mostar. So that is a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm just going to look for one of the reports where you said the exact opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm going to pose another objection at this point. I think there was a certain latitude that was related to Judge Clark's questions. I think now we are arguing the point way beyond the scope of Judge Clark's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, we believe that Judges could read all those reports and help you to solve this problem. And I can assure you that you have the full right to check with the recordings tonight or tomorrow, at a later stage. Now, we are running against time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I fully respect your ruling. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, in this organisational chart of this chain of command, did you ever find the name of my client anywhere? In this Exhibit 532.1, that is.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON WILLEM MARIA VAN DER GRINTEN
utterances.text: By my knowledge, he is not in this SpaBat diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Witness, for coming here to help us by giving your evidence. We all wish you a good trip back to your station.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. First off, the photograph of the -- well, particularly the three men identified, P36.1 modified for witness's markings, whichever slash that would be. Slash 1, I'm told. P417.1. P431.1. P435.1. P440.1. P451. P451.1. P452.1. P456.3. P456.4. P458.1. P462. P475. P476.2. P477. P480. P483. P484. P488. 497. P498. P516. P532.1. And, Your Honour, then the two photographs that were added, I'm told that that was once 893 has been corrected to 894. Is that correct? That was the photo of the vehicle -- what had previously been marked as Exhibit 894, the photograph of what the witness called the blue bank building has now been amended to be P895. And the Prosecution would tender all of those documents, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. And we would like our usual eight-day deadline for replying to this, except for the -- except the photographs, of course, to which we have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we object to P435.1, P477, and we will provide arguments because we believe that these pieces of paper prove nothing. And we do not object to the other exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe those photos have been admitted into the evidence since there's no objections from the Defence counsel. And the Defence counsel have eight days to submit their written objections on those issues. So tomorrow morning, there's no trial for this case because this courtroom is occupied by another case. But we have to be here at 2.15 in the afternoon. We'll sit until 7.00. We'll have that previous witness in the afternoon. So we'll resume at 2.15 tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
